subject.title: Add Gee runtime ownership envelope for OpenClaw

question: Should OpenClaw core own this Gee-specific hosted-runtime contract, or should the capability use a generic harness/plugin host-runtime seam?
rationale: Repairing the two concrete defects does not decide whether Gee-specific ownership types should become permanent contracts across core auth, tools, compaction, persistence, and Codex startup.

options.title: Use a generic host-runtime seam
options.body: Refactor the envelope into provider-neutral active-turn capabilities and credential-resolution hooks owned by the harness/plugin boundary.

options.title: Sponsor the Gee-specific contract
options.body: Keep Gee-specific core types only with explicit approval and complete compatibility, security, upgrade, and live-runtime proof.

options.title: Keep Gee outside core
options.body: Implement the integration in Gee-owned plugin or host code if existing OpenClaw seams are sufficient.

recommendation.title: Use a generic host-runtime seam
recommendation.body: Refactor the envelope into provider-neutral active-turn capabilities and credential-resolution hooks owned by the harness/plugin boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main history most directly connects this person to the affected auth, stream, and Codex lifecycle implementation.
